message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. He was born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, and rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School. LeBron was selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers and has since played for the Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers (again), and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Key highlights of his career include:

- **NBA Championships**: Four titles (2007 with the Cavaliers, 2012 & 2013 with the Heat, 2020 with the Lakers).
- **MVP Awards**: Four regular‑season MVPs (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and two Finals MVPs (2012, 2013).
- **All‑Star Appearances**: 19 selections, including multiple All‑NCAA and All‑NBA honors.
- **Scoring and Playmaking**: Known for his combination of size, athleticism, and skill, LeBron has consistently been among the league’s leaders in points, rebounds, and assists.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also known for his philanthropy—most notably the “I Promise” program, which supports at-risk youth in his hometown—and his ventures in entertainment and business, including production companies and endorsements. He remains a prominent figure in sports culture and a role model for many aspiring athletes.
